description: Passive rotational joint stiffness applied at runtime to the vendored MyoHand model. MyoHand defines joint damping but no stiffness; without it, a joint with any unopposed torque runs to its limit in zero gravity.
reference_posture: Each spring pulls toward the model reference posture qpos0 (all joints at 0 rad).
simplifications: Linear springs. Measured passive moments become exponential near the end of range.
Each degree of freedom is independent. Measured wrist and forearm stiffness is coupled.
Values are population means from small samples, not subject-specific.

In-vivo measurements include passive muscle-tendon stiffness, which the MyoHand muscle model also produces, so that share is counted twice. Kuo and Deshpande 2012 found muscle-tendon units contribute a limited share at the index MCP; the overlap was not quantified for other joints.

sources.citation: Formica D, Charles SK, Zollo L, Guglielmelli E, Hogan N, Krebs HI. The passive stiffness of the wrist and forearm. J Neurophysiol 108:1158-1166, 2012.
Shi XQ, Heung HL, Tang ZQ, Tong KY, Li Z. Verification of finger joint stiffness estimation method with soft robotic actuator. Front Bioeng Biotechnol 8:592637, 2020.
Kuo PH, Deshpande AD. Muscle-tendon units provide limited contributions to the passive stiffness of the index finger metacarpophalangeal joint. J Biomech 45:2531-2538, 2012.
Dionysian E, Kabo JM, Dorey FJ, Meals RA. Proximal interphalangeal joint stiffness: measurement and analysis. J Hand Surg Am 30:573-579, 2005.
Domalain M, Vigouroux L, Berton E. Determination of passive moment-angle relationships at the trapeziometacarpal joint. J Biomech Eng 132:071009, 2010.

A simulating analysis of the effects of increased joint stiffness on muscle loading in a thumb (PMC2804669). Simulation study; its thumb stiffness values are model assumptions, not measurements. Authors not re-checked here.

pro_sup_r.notes: Mean of 0.24 (toward pronation) and 0.19 (toward supination); n=10, about +/-0.8 rad. Linear fit is weak (R2 0.61).

deviation_r.notes: Diagonal of the 2-D wrist stiffness matrix; n=10, +/-0.3 rad. The coupling term with flexion (-0.18) is omitted.

flexion_r.notes: Diagonal of the 2-D wrist stiffness matrix; n=10. Measured stiffness toward extension (1.02) is about twice that toward flexion (0.55); one linear spring cannot capture that asymmetry.

cmc_flexion_r.notes: No linear in-vivo value found. Domalain 2010 reports a nonlinear moment-angle fit whose coefficients were not retrieved. Value matches a simulation study's assumption.

cmc_abduction_r.notes: Same basis as thumb CMC flexion.

mp_flexion_r.notes: No in-vivo measurement found; simulation-study assumption.

ip_flexion_r.notes: No in-vivo measurement found; simulation-study assumption.

mcp2_flexion_r.notes: Index MCP, 0.033-0.047 in controls (n=4, about 10-40 deg flexion). Other studies range 0.016-0.21; treat as order of magnitude.

mcp2_abduction_r.notes: No in-vivo abduction/adduction measurement found. Set to 1.5x the MCP flexion value.

pm2_flexion_r.notes: 0.05 N*cm/deg across index, middle, and ring PIP (n=89).

md2_flexion_r.notes: No DIP measurement found. Set to about half the PIP value.
